what: لا تقل «لا أستطيع» قبل أن تفحص خريطة القدرات وأدواتك وسجل الحزم، وتحاول التثبيت. — Never answer "I can't" until you have checked the capability map, your tool list, the package registry and an install attempt.
when: any request that sounds outside chat: render a video, OCR a scan, read a repo, build a PDF, call an API, use a library you think is missing; أي طلب يبدو مستحيلًا أو خارج المحادثة
how: 1) `python3 scripts/powers.py search <words>` in this skill; 2) scan your tool list and ToolSearch for deferred tools (SELF-05, SELF-06); 3) probe: `command -v X`, `python3 -c 'import X'`; 4) registry: `pip index versions X` or `npm view X version license`; 5) install into a venv or scratch folder and run the smallest example (SELF-26, SELF-27); 6) only then answer: done, needs a key (name it), or blocked (name the gate) plus the best keyless alternative.
params: max 6 steps before answering; a proxy 403/407 is a policy block: report it, never route around it

what: لكل قدرة حالة واحدة صادقة من فكرة إلى مُتحقَّق منها؛ أبلغ دائمًا بأدنى حالة صحيحة. — Every capability sits on one rung from idea to verified; always report the lowest rung that is true.
when: before you claim anything works, before giving a badge, when writing a final report
how: IDEA 💡 (no source) → DOCUMENTED 📄 (a file describes it with numbers) → INSTALLABLE 📦 (registry resolves through the proxy) → NEEDS-KEY 🔑 (name the key, account or connector) → PRESENT 🟢 (`command -v`, import or tool listed in this session) → EXECUTED (exit code and output path known) → VERIFIED ✅ (postcondition checked: ffprobe numbers, tests pass, file reopens, frame viewed). BLOCKED = named gate + next step. Never merge two rungs into a yes/no.

what: رسالة النجاح ليست دليلًا؛ افحص الشرط اللاحق على الناتج نفسه. — A success message is not evidence; check the postcondition on the artifact itself.
when: after any render, install, conversion, deploy or file write, before saying done
how: Pick the check by artifact. Video: `ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration:stream=codec_type,r_frame_rate`, then look at frames. Document: reopen it or convert it (`soffice --headless --convert-to pdf`). Code: run the tests. Web page: take a screenshot. Install: import it and print the version. Only an output from that check upgrades EXECUTED to VERIFIED.

what: اختبر مضيفين أو أكثر لتعرف مستوى الشبكة: كاملة، أو سجلات فقط، أو لا شيء. — Test a few hosts to learn the network level: full, registries only, or none.
when: before promising installs, downloads, web fetches or API calls
how: `curl -sS -o /dev/null -m 8 -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}\n' https://pypi.org/simple/` plus registry.npmjs.org, api.github.com, huggingface.co and a non-registry host (example.com). 200/200 means full egress; registry 200 with other hosts 403 means an allowlist; DNS failures or timeouts mean no network (API sandbox). In a cloud session also run `curl "$HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status"`. P8: all 7 hosts returned 200.
params: timeout 8 s per host · classify ok / policy-blocked (403, 407, CONNECT 502) / offline

what: البروكسي جزء من الأمان: لا تعطّل التحقق من TLS ولا تلغِ متغيره، والرفض 403 قرار سياسة. — The proxy is part of security: never disable TLS checks or unset it; a 403 is a policy decision.
when: TLS errors, 403/405/407, cut-off transfers, Node or Python clients that ignore the proxy
how: Read the container's proxy README if present and its status endpoint. Point clients at the CA bundle (`SSL_CERT_FILE`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`). Node fetch: try `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` (P9: plain and env-proxy fetch both returned 200 here). aiohttp needs `trust_env=True`. Plain HTTP_PROXY is unsupported. Report 403/407 to the user; do not retry or route around them.

what: اعرف أي مفاتيح موجودة من أسماء المتغيرات دون طباعة قيمها أبدًا. — Learn which keys exist from variable names, never printing values.

what: أحدث إصدار على PyPI قد لا يُثبَّت على بايثونك؛ اقرأ requires_python. — PyPI's latest release may not install on your Python; read requires_python.

how: `curl -s https://pypi.org/pypi/<pkg>/json | python3 -c "import json,sys; i=json.load(sys.stdin)['info']; print(i['version'], i['requires_python'])"` and compare with `pip index versions <pkg>`. Fixes: use the fork, an older pin, or `uv venv --python 3.12`.

what: اقرأ رخصة الحزمة من السجل أو ملف LICENSE قبل اعتمادها، وانتبه لـAGPL وGPL و«انظر الرخصة». — Read the license from the registry or LICENSE file before adopting; watch for AGPL, GPL and 'SEE LICENSE'.
when: choosing a library to bundle, vendor or ship; copying code or assets
how: npm: `npm view <pkg> license`. PyPI JSON: `license_expression`, else `license`, else the classifiers. GitHub: `curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<o>/<r>/HEAD/LICENSE | head -3`. Red flags: AGPL (pymupdf, ultralytics), GPL (piper-tts, pedalboard, bpy, typed.js, ffmpeg-static), 'SEE LICENSE IN …' (remotion, @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk), UNLICENSED, or blank. Using a tool to produce output differs from redistributing its code.

what: قبل كتابة شيء من الصفر ابحث عن حزمة أو أداة أو مهارة، ثم قرّر: تبنَّ، أو وسّع، أو ركّب، أو ابنِ. — Before writing from scratch, search for a package, tool or skill, then decide: adopt, extend, compose or build.
when: any feature, effect, parser, converter or integration you are about to hand-code
how: Search in parallel: this repo, then package registries, then MCP tools and skills, then GitHub templates. Score each candidate on fit, maintenance, docs, license and dependencies. Exact maintained match with a permissive license → Adopt. Partial match → Extend with a thin wrapper. Several weak matches → Compose 2-3 small packages. Nothing → Build, informed by what you found. Say which channels you skipped.

what: قبل إنشاء مهارة جديدة ابحث محليًا ثم في المتجر ثم في GitHub، وافحص ما تجد. — Before creating a new skill, search locally, then the marketplace, then GitHub, and vet what you find.

how: 1) Intent + 3-5 bilingual keywords. 2) Local: `find ~/.claude/skills .claude/skills -name SKILL.md | xargs grep -il <kw>`. 3) Account: ListSkills / SearchSkills / SearchPlugins. 4) Remote: GitHub search (in cloud sessions use `mcp__github__search_repositories`, since `gh search` is blocked, P13), plus at most 3 web queries. 5) Vet: unexpected shell, network, credential handling or installs; maintenance; license. 6) Rank (name match > description > local > maintained GitHub > web), cap 10, then offer use, fork, or create.

what: سمِّ العطل ثم طبّق أصغر إصلاح له، ولا تكرر الطلب نفسه بلا تغيير. — Name the failure, apply its smallest fix, and never resend an identical failing call.
when: a tool call, install, probe or subagent fails
how: STALE_STATE → re-probe. BAD_TOOL_ARGS → read the schema, fix once, never resend identical arguments. PROBE_ABORT → run independent probes separately. MISSING_DEP → install in isolation, then verify import and version. NEEDS_AUTH → name the key or connector. POLICY_BLOCK (403/407) → report it, no workaround. SUPPLY_CHAIN_RISK → read the source, do not run unknown installers or hooks. REGRESSION → roll back.
params: retry a failed piece once, narrower

how: Before the call, state what it will do, the cost if known (quote or balance tools first), and whether it can be undone. Get a yes, or rely on intent the user already stated.
